subject: Maths
title: Simplifying surds
subtitle: Surds · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can simplify surds by finding the largest square factor.

key_vocab.definition: To simplify a surd, find the largest perfect square factor of the number under the root sign and take its square root outside.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can simplify surds by finding the largest square factor.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: simplify a surd -- To simplify a surd, find the largest perfect square factor of the number under the root sign and take its square root outside.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Find the largest perfect square that divides the number. Take its root outside the radical.
√n = a√b where n = a² × b
b should have no perfect square factors left

Key examples:
  ✓ √12 = √(4 × 3) = 2√3  (4 is the square factor)
  ✓ √50 = √(25 × 2) = 5√2  (25 is the largest square factor)
  ✓ √72 = √(36 × 2) = 6√2  (36 is the largest square factor)
  ✗ √12 = √6 × √2  (not simplified; need square factors)
  ✗ √50 = √(10 × 5) = √10√5  (neither factor is a perfect square)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – basic simplification
  Simplify √20.
  Find largest square factor of 20: 4
  √20 = √(4 × 5)
  = 2√5
  2√5
  (4 is the largest perfect square that divides 20.)

Example 2 – larger number
  Simplify √45.
  Find largest square factor of 45: 9
  √45 = √(9 × 5)
  = 3√5
  3√5
  (9 is the largest perfect square that divides 45.)

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ √12 = 2√3 because 12 = 4 × 3
✗ √50 = 10√2
✓ √72 = 6√2 because 72 = 36 × 2
✗ √8 = 4√2
✓ A surd is fully simplified when no perfect square divides the radicand
